When Professor Holland left the chair of Mathematics in early 1887, Elihu R. Hinshaw, a native of Indiana, came to the faculty, first as Professor of Natural and Applied Mathematics, later as Professor of Mathematics and Natural Science, and Treasurer, and the associate editor of the College paper.

Mr. Hinshaw had received the A.B. degree in 1882, was considerably older than the other faculty members, and had been in college work for some years before coming to Savoy. His association with the College ran a little more than two years, and ended in 1890, when he was given the presidency of the Southeastern State Normal School at Durant, Oklahoma.
